column1: What three silicon tiles make up a Vera Rubin Superchip?
column2: Two Rubin GPUs and one Vera CPU, all packaged together on a single substrate.

column1: How many transistors does the Rubin GPU package total across both dies?
What process node is the Rubin GPU fabricated on?
How much HBM4 memory does the full Superchip carry?
column2: 576 GB — 288 GB per GPU × two GPUs.

column1: What is the FP4 compute performance of the full Superchip?
How does NVLink-C2C’s bandwidth compare to PCIe Gen6 x16?
column2: Roughly seven times higher — PCIe Gen6 delivers about 256 GB/s total bidirectional (128 GB/s per direction).

column1: What CPU architecture does the Vera CPU use?
column2: NVIDIA’s Olympus Arm v9 architecture, with 88 cores.

column1: How many components does a Vera Rubin Superchip contain?
column2: Roughly seventeen thousand — about five times the part count of a smartphone.

column1: What is the Vera CPU’s primary job in the Superchip?
column2: Coordination: managing GPU memory, dispatching kernels, handling I/O, running the OS, and communicating with other Superchips through the rack network.
